editor_note: The three rewritten entries (7, 63, 70) match their English: "valida ambos antes de enviar un job", "circuito ISA representativo" and "supresión y mitigación de errores basadas en los datos de caracterización" are all accurate, and job/backend/runtime are handled the same way as in the rest of the page.

The rewritten benchmark table (entry 39) matches the English: every qubit count, initialization, error and time value carries over, and the rows use the same names as the prose ("Ecuación de Burgers no viscosa", "Ecuaciones de Euler sin presión"). There is one small problem. The third row says "Prueba de tracción 1D hipoelástica", but entry 27 says "ensayo de tracción unidimensional". "Ensayo de tracción" is the standard Spanish materials-testing term, so the table should use it too.

examples.source: Hypoelastic 1D tensile test
examples.translation: Prueba de tracción 1D hipoelástica
examples.suggested: Ensayo de tracción 1D hipoelástico
examples.why: Entry 27 uses the conventional term 'ensayo de tracción', so 'Prueba de tracción' here is inconsistent within the page. 'Ensayo' is also the standard word in Spanish materials engineering. Changing the noun also changes the adjective to the masculine 'hipoelástico'.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 6 is faithful and natural: it keeps the meaning of every clause, including "Bloque Unificado Primitivo (PUB)", run() "ejecuta la carga de trabajo definida como un trabajo", and results that depend on "tanto de los PUBs utilizados como de las opciones de runtime", and "opciones de runtime" matches the rest of the file.

All three rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entries 7 and 8 are faithful: "ventana deslizante de 28 días", "a partir de hace 28 días" and "ciertos códigos de error conocidos" are all accurate, and the Flex Plan caveat is kept in both. The problems are in entry 10, which is stiff in two places. "IBM asigna una asignación" repeats the same word and reads like a word-for-word copy of the English. "se distribuyan equitativamente entre cada instancia" is awkward Spanish and should be "entre las instancias" or "a cada instancia". Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: IBM® assigns an allocation of quantum computing capacity to the IBM Cloud account of each organization
examples.translation: IBM® asigna una asignación de capacidad de computación cuántica a la cuenta de IBM Cloud de cada organización
examples.suggested: IBM® otorga a la cuenta de IBM Cloud de cada organización una asignación de capacidad de computación cuántica
examples.why: "asigna una asignación" repeats the same word and copies the English too literally. A native technical writer would use a different verb.

examples.source: in a manner that fairly distributes resources to each instance
examples.translation: de manera que los recursos se distribuyan equitativamente entre cada instancia
examples.suggested: de manera que los recursos se distribuyan equitativamente entre las instancias
examples.why: "entre cada" is awkward in Spanish. "entre" needs a plural noun, or you use "a cada instancia" instead.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The register is consistently informal (tú). The main problem is that "runtime jobs" is translated two ways: "trabajos de tiempo de ejecución" in [55]–[56] and "trabajos de runtime" / "servicio de runtime" in [57]. Also, the link text "Managing user API keys" / "IBM Cloud API keys" stays in English in [25] but is translated in [27]. In [43], "La función se está optimizando" reads as though the function itself is being optimized, when the English means the function is doing the optimizing.

examples.source: A function reports its runtime jobs only when it submits them through the runtime service
examples.translation: Una función informa de sus trabajos de runtime solo cuando los envía a través del servicio de runtime
examples.suggested: Una función informa de sus trabajos de tiempo de ejecución solo cuando los envía a través del servicio de tiempo de ejecución (o usar 'runtime' en [55]–[57] por igual)
examples.why: [55]–[56] say 'trabajos de tiempo de ejecución' for the same concept, so the file uses two terms for one thing.

examples.source: The function is optimizing for the selected QPU.
examples.translation: La función se está optimizando para la QPU seleccionada.
examples.suggested: La función está optimizando la carga de trabajo para la QPU seleccionada.
examples.why: The reflexive 'se está optimizando' suggests the function itself is being optimized. The English means the function is doing the optimizing.

examples.source: Learn more in the [Managing user API keys] topic.
examples.translation: Obtén más información en el tema [Managing user API keys]
examples.suggested: Obtén más información en el tema [Gestión de claves de API de usuario]
examples.why: The same link text is translated in [27] ('Gestión de claves de API de usuario', 'claves de API de IBM Cloud'), so the two passages should match.

editor_note: Entry 60 keeps the English meaning. Dynamical decoupling is correctly given as "desacoplamiento dinámico", and the trade-off (higher levels mean more accurate results but longer processing) is intact, so a learner would not be misled. Two things still need an edit. "especifica cuánta resiliencia construir contra errores" copies the English "build resilience against" word for word and reads stiffly in Spanish. The link label "Error mitigation and suppression techniques" was left in English, while every other link label on the page is translated.

examples.source: The resilience level specifies how much resilience to build against errors.
examples.translation: El nivel de resiliencia especifica cuánta resiliencia construir contra errores.
examples.suggested: El nivel de resiliencia especifica cuánta protección frente a errores se aplica.
examples.why: The infinitive 'construir' copies 'to build' literally and 'contra' copies 'against', which is stiff. A native technical writer would use 'frente a errores' and a passive 'se aplica' / 'se incorpora'.

examples.source: see [Error mitigation and suppression techniques](/guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques)
examples.translation: consulta [Error mitigation and suppression techniques](/guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques)
examples.suggested: consulta [Técnicas de mitigación y supresión de errores](/guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques)
examples.why: Every other link label on the page is translated (e.g. 'Inicio rápido', 'guardado tus credenciales'), so this English label is inconsistent.

editor_note: The rewritten method table in entry 11 keeps the meaning of the English: "llamada bloqueante hasta que se complete" and "Bloquea hasta que el trabajo alcance un estado terminal" say the same thing as the source. It does switch "job" to "trabajo" in all four rows, though. Every other entry on the page keeps "job", including entry 10 just before the table ("La instancia de job") and entry 12 just after it ("El estado de tu job"). The table should use "job" to match the rest of the page.

examples.source: | `job.status()` | Check the current job status |
examples.translation: | `job.status()` | Consulta el estado actual del trabajo |
examples.suggested: | `job.status()` | Consulta el estado actual del job | (and likewise "identificador único del job", "resultados del job", "hasta que el job alcance un estado terminal")
examples.why: Every other entry on the page keeps "job" (entries 0-46). Using "trabajo" only in this table is a within-file inconsistency. The concept is still clear, so it will not mislead a learner.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, with informal tú held throughout ("Aprende cómo involucrarte", "Al unirte a la comunidad"), a consistent open-source rendering ("apertura del código fuente", "ecosistema Qiskit de código abierto") and defensible kept loanwords ("framework", "pull requests").

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. Entry 27 keeps the claim that the primitives are "más sofisticada... como servicio en la nube" and are used to access IBM Quantum hardware. Entry 34 keeps the hedge "es posible que puedas acceder con mayor facilidad", renders "mitigación y supresión de errores" and "activando opciones como el resilience_level" correctly, and keeps the "primitivos" term consistent.

Entry 8 is faithful and natural: "se desarrolló utilizando los siguientes requisitos" and "Te recomendamos usar estas versiones o más recientes" keep both the minimum-version meaning and the informal tú register.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: entry 3 keeps the caveat about error mitigation ("con mitigación de errores incluida") and says "valores de expectación", matching the Estimator card. Entry 9 uses "clases base de primitivos" and informal "Aprende/Revisa/Consulta" throughout.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The IBM and user responsibilities are never swapped, and the "IBM no es responsable de la copia de seguridad…" caveats in the disaster-recovery table are kept. The one visible defect is in entry [17]: "nuevas instancias de IBM Quantum Compute Service [instances](/guides/instances)" says "instances" twice and leaves the link text in English, so the link should go on "instancias". Two smaller points: "impactan a los clientes" is a calque (use "afectan a los clientes"), and in [15] the "any" in "any public networks" was dropped ("en redes públicas").

examples.source: Provision new IBM Quantum Compute Service [instances](/guides/instances) in an alternate region, if available.
examples.translation: Aprovisionar nuevas instancias de IBM Quantum Compute Service [instances](/guides/instances) en una región alternativa, si está disponible.
examples.suggested: Aprovisionar nuevas [instancias](/guides/instances) de IBM Quantum Compute Service en una región alternativa, si está disponible.
examples.why: The noun appears twice, once in Spanish and once as English link text, so the sentence is duplicated and part of it is not translated.

examples.source: Post notifications for changes that impact customers.
examples.translation: Publicar notificaciones sobre los cambios que impactan a los clientes.
examples.suggested: Publicar notificaciones sobre los cambios que afectan a los clientes.
examples.why: 'Impactar a' copies the English 'impact'. In technical Spanish, 'afectar a' is the natural verb here, and entry [15] already uses it.

examples.source: Encrypt data when it is transmitted on any public networks
examples.translation: Cifrar los datos cuando se transmiten en redes públicas
examples.suggested: Cifrar los datos cuando se transmiten por cualquier red pública
examples.why: The universal quantifier 'any' was dropped. This is a small loss of emphasis and would not mislead a reader.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The translation uses tú consistently, and backend, runtime, transpilar and carga de trabajo are rendered the same way everywhere, so nothing here would mislead a learner. There are three calques a native editor would fix. In [31], "registra … frente al trabajo padre" translates "against" literally, and "frente a" reads as "opposite/versus" rather than "under/attached to". In [15], "transpilará un circuit contra un backend" is a similar calque of "against", where "para un backend" is the natural Spanish. In [40], "que se sube y luego se limpia" is stiff when said of a tar file, which in Spanish "se elimina".

examples.source: registers every IBM Quantum primitive job and session it launches against the parent Qiskit Serverless job
examples.translation: registra cada trabajo y sesión de primitivas de IBM Quantum que lanza frente al trabajo padre de Qiskit Serverless
examples.suggested: registra cada trabajo y sesión de primitivas de IBM Quantum que lanza, asociándolos al trabajo padre de Qiskit Serverless
examples.why: 'frente a' is a literal calque of 'against'. It suggests opposition or comparison, not being attached to something, which slightly obscures what the wrapper does.

examples.source: will transpile a `circuit` against a given `backend` and target `optimization_level`
examples.translation: transpilará un `circuit` contra un `backend` dado y un `optimization_level` objetivo
examples.suggested: transpilará un `circuit` para un `backend` dado con un `optimization_level` objetivo
examples.why: 'transpilar contra' is an English calque. A Spanish technical writer would say 'para' here.

examples.source: into a `tar`, which is uploaded and then cleaned up
examples.translation: en un archivo `tar`, que se sube y luego se limpia
examples.suggested: en un archivo `tar`, que se sube y luego se elimina
examples.why: 'limpiar' a file is a literal rendering of 'clean up'. The intended meaning is that the temporary archive is deleted.

editor_note: Entry 6 keeps the English meaning accurately. It keeps the caveat that the reference primitives do not model noise and that Aer's primitives "sí lo admiten", and nothing is added or left out. The one change a native editor would make is the linked title "primitivas de Qiskit SDK". That follows English word order, and entry 21 already gives the same guide title as "primitivas del SDK de Qiskit", so the page names that guide in two different ways. "que obtendrías" for "you would expect" is a defensible, slightly more direct rendering.

examples.source: [Exact simulation with Qiskit SDK primitives](/guides/simulate-with-qiskit-sdk-primitives) demonstrates
examples.translation: [La simulación exacta con primitivas de Qiskit SDK](/guides/simulate-with-qiskit-sdk-primitives) muestra
examples.suggested: [La simulación exacta con primitivas del SDK de Qiskit](/guides/simulate-with-qiskit-sdk-primitives) muestra
examples.why: "Qiskit SDK" follows English word order; natural Spanish is "SDK de Qiskit". Using that here would also match how entry 21 renders the same guide title.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and natural overall, and it uses terms consistently: "corrección de errores cuánticos", "código de Shor de 9 qubits", "discretización de errores" and tú-register ("te guía", "puedes", "Descarga"). There are two small shifts. In [3], "possibly don't exist" becomes "posiblemente nunca existirán". That turns a statement about whether such algorithms exist at all into a prediction about the future. In [5], "a key tool" is softened to "una herramienta importante", which loses the idea that error correction is the enabling tool. Neither shift would mislead a learner.

examples.source: for which efficient classical algorithms are not known, and possibly don't exist
examples.translation: para las que no se conocen algoritmos clásicos eficientes — y posiblemente nunca existirán
examples.suggested: para las que no se conocen algoritmos clásicos eficientes, y posiblemente no existan
examples.why: The English says such algorithms may not exist at all. "Nunca existirán" ("will never exist") turns this into a prediction about the future and makes it slightly stronger.

examples.source: we have a key tool to help us in this endeavor
examples.translation: contamos con una herramienta importante que puede ayudarnos
examples.suggested: contamos con una herramienta clave para esta empresa
examples.why: "Key" becomes "importante" and "to help us" becomes the hedged "que puede ayudarnos", so the central role of error correction comes across weaker.

editor_note: Entry 9 is faithful. The condition (p too large means no help and possibly worse), the 3.23% figure with its "or so" hedge, and the point that the fault-tolerant circuit has more locations where errors can occur all come through intact. The one slip is "por encima de aproximadamente 3,23%". Spanish needs the article before a percentage, so a native editor would write "por encima del 3,23 % aproximadamente". The terms "código de Shor de $9$ qubits" and "implementación tolerante a fallos" match the rest of the page.

examples.source: if the error probability is above 3.23% or so
examples.translation: si la probabilidad de error está por encima de aproximadamente 3,23%
examples.suggested: si la probabilidad de error supera el 3,23 % aproximadamente
examples.why: Spanish percentages take the definite article ("el/del 3,23 %"), and putting "aproximadamente" between the preposition and the number reads like a word-for-word calque. The meaning is correct.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall. The key exam facts all carry over correctly: 20 questions, at least 16 correct to pass ("al menos 16"), and a temporary lock after two failed attempts. Two small drifts are left. First, "badging exam" in [7] and the title in [1] both become "examen final", which drops the link between passing the exam and earning the badge and adds a "final" that the English does not have. Second, the legal notice in [12] renders "to assist in the administration" as "para administrar", which says Credly runs the whole program rather than just helping with it, and uses the calque "procesador de datos" where Spanish privacy wording would say "encargado del tratamiento de datos".

examples.source: where you can take the badging exam for Fundamentals of quantum algorithms
examples.translation: donde podrás realizar el examen final de Fundamentos de algoritmos cuánticos
examples.suggested: donde podrás realizar el examen para obtener la insignia de Fundamentos de algoritmos cuánticos
examples.why: 'badging exam' means the exam that awards the badge. 'examen final' drops that link and adds a 'final' that the English does not say.

examples.source: Exam for Fundamentals of quantum algorithms
examples.translation: Examen final de Fundamentos de algoritmos cuánticos
examples.suggested: Examen de Fundamentos de algoritmos cuánticos
examples.why: The added word 'final' is not in the source.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM ... to assist in the administration of the IBM Digital Badge program
examples.translation: un procesador de datos externo autorizado por IBM ... para administrar el programa IBM Digital Badge
examples.suggested: un encargado del tratamiento de datos externo autorizado por IBM ... para ayudar en la administración del programa IBM Digital Badge
examples.why: 'procesador de datos' is a calque; standard Spanish privacy wording is 'encargado del tratamiento'. 'para administrar' overstates Credly's role, since the source says it only helps.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 5 and 12 are faithful and natural. Entry 12 correctly keeps "tu insignia", "realiza el examen" and "Credly te notificará", all in the tú register. Entry 17 has two calque-level slips. "third-party data processor" became "procesador de datos externo", but the usual Spanish privacy term is "encargado del tratamiento de datos". "emitirte una IBM Digital Badge" puts a feminine article on the English program name, which reads awkwardly; "emitirte una insignia digital de IBM" would be better.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: un procesador de datos externo autorizado por IBM
examples.suggested: un encargado del tratamiento de datos externo autorizado por IBM
examples.why: 'Procesador de datos' is a literal calque. Spanish privacy and legal texts (RGPD/GDPR) use 'encargado del tratamiento'.

examples.source: In order to issue you an IBM Digital Badge
examples.translation: Para poder emitirte una IBM Digital Badge
examples.suggested: Para poder emitirte una insignia digital de IBM
examples.why: Putting a feminine article in front of the English program name reads awkwardly. It is better to keep the program name for 'programa IBM Digital Badge' and use 'insignia digital' for the badge itself.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 16, 70 and 108 are accurate and read naturally: "entornos de cómputo heterogéneos", "frecuencia de reloj", "superposición de 0 y 1" and the CLOPS gloss all match the English. The one problem is in entry 6, the video title. It opens a range with "hasta" but has no "desde" before it ("se aplican a sistemas simples como una computadora portátil hasta entornos HPC heterogéneos"), so the laptop-to-HPC range reads as broken. A native editor would fix that.

examples.source: that apply to simple systems like a laptop all the way up to heterogeneous HPC environments
examples.translation: que se aplican a sistemas simples como una computadora portátil hasta entornos HPC heterogéneos
examples.suggested: que se aplican desde sistemas simples, como una computadora portátil, hasta entornos HPC heterogéneos
examples.why: The range has 'hasta' with no matching 'desde', so the phrase reads broken. It also loses the 'all the way up to' sense of scale.

editor_note: Neither rewritten entry misleads the reader. Entry 15 is faithful and matches the page's wording ("preparadas para lo cuántico", as in "Cómo prepararse para lo cuántico"). Entry 17 carries the meaning of all four capability bullets, but a native editor would still fix two things. It says "valor de negocio" where the rest of the page uses "valor empresarial" (entries 25, 31, 34), and "conocimientos accionables" is a stiff calque of "actionable insights". The last bullet, "Influencia de las regulaciones", copies the English ambiguity word for word; "Influencia en las regulaciones" would make clear that this is the organization's own capability.

examples.source: Proficiency to capture business value from quantum-triggered strategies
examples.translation: Competencia para capturar valor de negocio a partir de estrategias
examples.suggested: Competencia para generar valor empresarial a partir de estrategias
examples.why: The rest of the page says 'valor empresarial' for 'business value' (entries 25, 31, 34). 'Capturar valor' is also a calque.

examples.source: convert quantum market information into actionable insights on opportunities and threats
examples.translation: convertir la información del mercado cuántico en conocimientos accionables sobre oportunidades y amenazas
examples.suggested: convertir la información del mercado cuántico en conclusiones prácticas sobre oportunidades y amenazas
examples.why: 'Conocimientos accionables' is a translationese calque of 'actionable insights'. A native business writer would more likely write 'conclusiones prácticas' or 'información útil para la toma de decisiones'.

examples.source: Influence of regulations and standards related to the intended use of quantum computing.
examples.translation: Influencia de las regulaciones y los estándares relacionados con el uso previsto de la computación cuántica.
examples.suggested: Influencia en las regulaciones y los estándares relacionados con el uso previsto de la computación cuántica.
examples.why: The list describes what the organization is able to do, so the point is its influence on regulations. 'Influencia de' reads as the influence regulations have. The English is equally ambiguous, so this is minor, not a meaning drift.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries (17, 24, 30, 35, 36, 39) would mislead a learner. The meaning holds in all of them, including the optimization-level explanation and the skip_transpilation caveat. The problems are calques a native editor would fix: "el primitivo SDK de Qiskit, Estimator" and the passive "el valor a ser minimizado" (30), "hemos establecido resiliencia a 0" and "ejecución de hardware" (39), and the unbalanced "siendo 0 sin optimización, y 1 … indicando" (36). In entry 35 the label "Sessions:" stays in English while the text says "sesiones", and "trabajo" is used where the rest of the page says "job" (entries 34, 40).

examples.source: the most efficient way to do that is using the Qiskit SDK primitive, Estimator ... (since that is the value to be minimized)
examples.translation: es usando el primitivo SDK de Qiskit, Estimator ... (puesto que ese es el valor a ser minimizado)
examples.suggested: es usar la primitiva Estimator del SDK de Qiskit ... (puesto que es el valor que queremos minimizar)
examples.why: This copies the English word order: 'primitivo SDK' reads as if SDK modifies the noun, and 'a ser minimizado' is a known anglicism in Spanish.

examples.source: For this first hardware run, we have set resilience to 0
examples.translation: Para esta primera ejecución de hardware, hemos establecido resiliencia a 0
examples.suggested: Para esta primera ejecución en hardware, hemos fijado el nivel de resiliencia en 0
examples.why: Spanish needs the article and 'en' here; 'ejecución de hardware' sounds like the run is about the hardware rather than on it.

examples.source: with 0 indicating no optimization, and 1 (the default) indicating some optimization
examples.translation: siendo 0 sin optimización, y 1 (el valor predeterminado) indicando cierta optimización
examples.suggested: donde 0 indica que no hay optimización y 1 (el valor predeterminado) aplica cierta optimización
examples.why: The two halves of the construction do not match, which makes the sentence read stiffly.

examples.source: Sessions: ... prior to the job's start
examples.translation: Sessions: ... previa al inicio del trabajo
examples.suggested: Sesiones: ... antes del inicio del job
examples.why: The label stays in English while the text says 'sesiones', and 'trabajo' breaks with 'job', which entries 34 and 40 use.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 65 is faithful and natural: "Predecirlas con precisión es crucial no solo para comprender el ADN y nuestros genes, sino también para diseñar terapias basadas en ARN, como la vacuna contra el COVID-19" keeps the not-only/but-also structure and uses ARNm/ARN consistently with the rest of the page.

Entry 44's video title is faithful and natural ("ofrece un breve repaso de las redes neuronales y de cómo los circuitos cuánticos pueden formar estructuras análogas"), and "video" matches the page's Latin American convention, which also uses "computadoras".

Neither rewritten entry misleads a learner. The depth thresholds (10 or fewer, 50-60 state of the art), the caveat that classical kernels would likely also reach 100%, and the "QKE works but is not quantum advantage" point all come through intact. In entry 76, the last bullet renders "expect to hold on real quantum computers" as "esperas ver". That changes "trends that stay true" into "trends you will observe", a slight shift. "¿Se aplica a tipos de datos amplios...?" is also a stiff calque. In entry 52, "En el medio" is calqued from "In between" and would read better as "Entre ambos valores" or "En el rango intermedio".

examples.source: Which trends, if any, do you expect to hold on real quantum computers?
examples.translation: ¿Qué tendencias, si las hay, esperas ver en computadoras cuánticas reales?
examples.suggested: ¿Qué tendencias, si las hay, esperas que se mantengan en computadoras cuánticas reales?
examples.why: 'hold' asks whether the simulated trends stay true on hardware; 'esperas ver' only asks what you will observe, which loses the comparison with the simulator results.

examples.source: Does it hold for broad types of data or just this specific training data?
examples.translation: ¿Se aplica a tipos de datos amplios o solo a estos datos de entrenamiento específicos?
examples.suggested: ¿Se mantiene para una amplia variedad de tipos de datos o solo para estos datos de entrenamiento concretos?
examples.why: 'tipos de datos amplios' is a word-for-word calque, and 'se mantiene' fits 'hold' better than 'se aplica'.

examples.source: In between, your results may vary with data similarity...
examples.translation: En el medio, tus resultados pueden variar según la similitud de los datos...
examples.suggested: Entre ambos valores, tus resultados pueden variar según la similitud de los datos...
examples.why: 'En el medio' is calqued from 'In between' and does not make clear that it means the depth range between 10 and 50-60.

editor_note: Faithful and natural, with correct terms throughout ("supresión, mitigación, detección y corrección de errores cuánticos", "ventaja cuántica"), a good idiomatic rendering of "time-released" as "se publican de forma escalonada", and a consistent informal "Explora".

The page is faithful overall and uses the informal "tú" throughout ("Si eres nuevo/a", "Descarga el PDF"). Entry [9] turns "in achieving useful quantum computing" into "como introducción a la computación cuántica útil", which changes the goal from reaching useful quantum computing to getting an introduction to it. The claim is mild and non-technical, so a learner would not be misled. Entry [0] leaves out a verb, so "un curso en vivo en la Universidad" reads awkwardly, and "estimaciones honestas" in [8] is a stiff rendering of "good-faith estimates".

examples.source: useful to you and your students in achieving useful quantum computing
examples.translation: útiles para ti y tus estudiantes como introducción a la computación cuántica útil
examples.suggested: útiles para ti y tus estudiantes en el camino hacia una computación cuántica útil
examples.why: 'como introducción' is not in the source. The English speaks of achieving useful quantum computing, not of being introduced to it.

examples.source: based on a live course held at the University of Tokyo in 2024
examples.translation: basado en un curso en vivo en la Universidad de Tokio del año 2024
examples.suggested: basado en un curso presencial impartido en la Universidad de Tokio en 2024
examples.why: The participle 'held' is missing ('impartido'/'que tuvo lugar'), so the Spanish reads choppy. Entry [3] handles the same phrase correctly.

examples.source: Good-faith estimates of required QPU time have been provided
examples.translation: se proporcionaron estimaciones honestas del tiempo de QPU necesario
examples.suggested: se incluyen estimaciones aproximadas del tiempo de QPU necesario
examples.why: 'estimaciones honestas' is a literal calque of 'good-faith'. In this context the idea is a best-effort approximation.

editor_note: Entry 12 (the Credly privacy notice) is faithful overall and would not mislead a learner, but two details in this legal text drift slightly. "third-party data processor" is flattened to "proveedor externo", which drops the data-protection role. The Spanish term is "encargado del tratamiento de datos". Also, "It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices" becomes "Esto se realiza de acuerdo con…", which ties the privacy guarantee to the act of sharing instead of to how the personal data itself is handled.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM and located in the United States
examples.translation: un proveedor externo autorizado por IBM con sede en Estados Unidos
examples.suggested: un encargado externo del tratamiento de datos autorizado por IBM con sede en Estados Unidos
examples.why: 'Data processor' is a legal data-protection role (GDPR: encargado del tratamiento). 'Proveedor externo' loses that meaning in a privacy notice.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Esto se realiza de acuerdo con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.suggested: Dichos datos se tratarán de acuerdo con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.why: In the English, 'It' is the personal information and the promise is about how it is handled. 'Esto se realiza' reads as if only the sharing follows IBM's privacy practices.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (18, 22, 52, 53) would mislead a learner. Entries 22 ("justo al lado del notebook principal"), 52 and 53 are faithful and read naturally. The one problem is in entry 18: it copies the English participle chain as "..., exponiendo el flujo de trabajo completo ... y extendiéndolo con ...". That is a gerund-of-consequence construction that Spanish style guides reject, and a native technical editor would split it into a finite clause. All the facts in entry 18 are kept: the citation, the Heartwood attribution, geometry optimization, automatic qubit layout selection and the joint Cleveland Clinic/IBM authorship.

examples.source: exposing the full workflow for implicit solvent calculations and extending it with iterative solvent self-consistency
examples.translation: exponiendo el flujo de trabajo completo para los cálculos de solvente implícito y extendiéndolo con autoconsistencia iterativa del solvente
examples.suggested: (...5788-5796). El tutorial expone el flujo de trabajo completo para los cálculos de solvente implícito y lo amplía con autoconsistencia iterativa del solvente
examples.why: It copies the English participle chain as a gerund of consequence, which is a recognized Spanish style fault. Rewriting it as a finite clause reads natively and keeps the meaning.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The approximations section, the differential measurement protocol and the atol trade-off all keep their caveats and quantities, and core terms are used consistently (hamiltoniano, compuertas, qubits, teoría de calibre de red, trotterizado). The minor slips: [22] renders "every basis state is physical" as "todo estado base es físico", which a learner could misread as "ground state" (estado base), so "estado de la base" would be clearer. [92] leaves the label "The original paper:" in English. [66] writes "14,000" with an English thousands separator.

examples.source: In the LSH basis, Gauss's law is satisfied automatically by construction, so every basis state is physical.
examples.translation: En la base LSH, la ley de Gauss se satisface automáticamente por construcción, por lo que todo estado base es físico.
examples.suggested: ...por lo que todo estado de la base es físico.
examples.why: 'Estado base' is often read in Spanish as the ground state; 'estado de la base' clearly means a basis state.

examples.source: [1] The original paper: Ilčić, Majumdar, Mathew et al. ...
examples.translation: [1] The original paper: Ilčić, Majumdar, Mathew et al. ...
examples.suggested: [1] El artículo original: Ilčić, Majumdar, Mathew et al. ...
examples.why: The label before the citation is left untranslated. Only the paper title itself should stay in English.

examples.source: over 3400 two-qubit gates and 14,000 single-qubit gates
examples.translation: más de 3400 compuertas de dos qubits y 14,000 compuertas de un solo qubit
examples.suggested: más de 3400 compuertas de dos qubits y 14 000 compuertas de un solo qubit
examples.why: This is the English thousands separator. In Spanish, '14,000' can read as a decimal, and '3400' next to it uses no separator at all, so the two numbers are inconsistent.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the variational-bound, noise-tolerance, first-order-angle and M_J-product arguments, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problems are consistency and a few leftover strings. "shot" is "disparo" in [23]/[30] but "shot" from [105] on. "pooled SQD" also appears as "SQD agrupado". "Hamiltoniano" and "hamiltoniano" are both used. The Background anchor is "Contexto" in [20]/[92] but "Antecedentes" in [104]. "núcleo" stands for both nucleus and inert core in [21], and later "core" is used ([165]). "conjunto" covers both the excitation pool and the circuit ensemble ([0], [11]). The prose sentences in references [180] and [184] were left in English. In [165], "a few percent" became "unos pocos puntos porcentuales".

examples.source: a few *valence* nucleons moving ... above an inert *core*
examples.translation: un núcleo como unos pocos nucleones de *valencia* ... sobre un *núcleo* inerte
examples.suggested: ... sobre un *core* (carozo) inerte
examples.why: Using 'núcleo' for both the nucleus and the core in the same sentence blurs the difference, and [165] later uses 'core'.

examples.source: takes each shot that has the wrong number
examples.translation: toma cada shot que tiene un número incorrecto
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for the whole file ('shot' or 'disparo'), since [23] and [30] use 'disparo'.
examples.why: The same term is rendered two different ways in one file.

examples.source: described in the [Background](#background) section
examples.translation: descritas en la sección de [Antecedentes](#background)
examples.suggested: descritas en la sección [Contexto](#background)
examples.why: The heading was translated as 'Contexto' ([20]), so this link text doesn't match the section it points to.

examples.source: Source of the measured $2^+$ excitation energies quoted in Step 1.
examples.translation: Source of the measured $2^+$ excitation energies quoted in Step 1.
examples.suggested: Fuente de las energías de excitación $2^+$ medidas citadas en el Paso 1.
examples.why: This explanatory sentence in the reference entry wasn't translated. [180] has the same problem ('The embedded usda.snt file carries...').

examples.source: how the choice affects the ensemble's two-qubit depth
examples.translation: afecta la profundidad de dos qubits del conjunto
examples.suggested: afecta la profundidad de dos qubits del ensemble de circuitos
examples.why: 'conjunto' is also used for the excitation pool, so a reader can't tell ensemble from pool here. Later entries do keep 'ensemble'.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally in Spanish. Entry 15 says "función de pérdida ... de valores esperados de Pauli que imita la función objetivo original de max-cut" and "solucionador de optimización cuántico-clásico". Entry 59 keeps the informal tú register in "Responde esta breve encuesta ... Tus opiniones nos ayudarán".

All six rewritten entries (4, 20, 21, 27, 33, 74) keep the English meaning. The noise factors, the gate-folding formula, the three PEA learning steps and the amplifier options all survive, and entry 4 uses tú correctly ("Tu tiempo de ejecución puede variar"). The table in entry 27 names the method "Plegado de compuertas", but the next paragraph, entry 29 (not rewritten), says "El plegado de puertas (gate folding)". The same technique gets two names in back-to-back entries, and the rest of the page also mixes puertas and compuertas. Entry 74 reads stiffly because "con twirl" appears twice in one clause ("el modelo de ruido con twirl de Pauli para capas de compuertas base de dos qubits con twirl").

examples.source: **Gate folding** | Repeat gates in identity cycles
examples.translation: **Plegado de compuertas** | Repetir compuertas en ciclos de identidad
examples.suggested: Use one term for gate across the page, e.g. "Plegado de puertas" to match entry 29 ("El plegado de puertas (gate folding)") and entries 28, 59-61.
examples.why: The same technique is named two ways in adjacent entries (compuertas in the table, puertas in the next paragraph), so a learner may think these are different methods. This is a consistency problem, and nothing in the text is actually wrong.

examples.source: after learning the Pauli-twirled noise model for layers of twirled two-qubit basis gates
examples.translation: después de aprender el modelo de ruido con twirl de Pauli para capas de compuertas base de dos qubits con twirl
examples.suggested: después de aprender el modelo de ruido (con twirling de Pauli) de las capas de puertas base de dos qubits sometidas a twirling
examples.why: Repeating "con twirl" twice in one clause is clunky and copies the English word order. The meaning is kept, but it reads like machine translation.

editor_note: The meaning holds up throughout. The sampling-overhead figures (γ²=100 vs ≈6.3, 16x), the postselection formula, the conditions on the non-Markovian checks and the claims about convergence all match the English, and the Spanish keeps its terms consistent (valores esperados, posselección, sobrecosto de muestreo, qubits mediadores). A native editor would change two calques. In [25], a graph "edge" is rendered as "borde" where Spanish uses "arista". In [7], [33] and [34], "prune the noise model of terms" becomes "podar el modelo de ruido de los términos", which copies the English structure and reads awkwardly.

examples.source: If both qubits on an edge fail the check, the sample is discarded.
examples.translation: Si ambos qubits de un borde fallan la comprobación, la muestra se descarta.
examples.suggested: Si ambos qubits de una arista fallan la comprobación, la muestra se descarta.
examples.why: In graph and coupling-map contexts, the conventional Spanish term for an edge is "arista". "Borde" means a border or rim.

examples.source: This mask will be used to prune the noise model of detectable terms before performing PEC.
examples.translation: Esta máscara se usará para podar el modelo de ruido de los términos detectables antes de realizar PEC.
examples.suggested: Esta máscara se usará para eliminar del modelo de ruido los términos detectables antes de realizar PEC.
examples.why: This copies the English "prune X of Y" pattern. In Spanish, "podar ... de" is awkward and could briefly be misread as a genitive ("the model of the terms").

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout. The PQK rationale in [13], the geometric-separation and model-complexity conditions in [58] (order √N, "sustancialmente menor que N") and the 80-minute QPU caveat all match the English. Terminology is consistent: núcleo cuántico proyectado, cúbit, 1-RDM, valores esperados, mapa de características. The file mostly uses informal "tú", but three spots slip into usted: the title imperative "Mejore" [1], "Su tiempo de ejecución" [3], and "los archivos que descargó" [52], which sits next to "Si realizaste". There are also small stylistic points: "Hamiltoniano" is capitalized where Spanish writes "hamiltoniano", and "diseñado en las células T" [29] is a calque.

examples.source: Enhance feature classification using projected quantum kernels
examples.translation: Mejore la clasificación de características utilizando núcleos cuánticos proyectados
examples.suggested: Mejora la clasificación de características con núcleos cuánticos proyectados
examples.why: Formal usted imperative; the page otherwise uses tú.

examples.source: Your runtime might vary.
examples.translation: Su tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.suggested: Tu tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.why: Formal possessive breaks the tú convention.

examples.source: which are included in the files you downloaded
examples.translation: que se incluyen en los archivos que descargó
examples.suggested: que se incluyen en los archivos que descargaste
examples.why: Formal verb form in the same paragraph as 'Si realizaste', so the register is inconsistent within one paragraph.

examples.source: 1D-Heisenberg Hamiltonian evolution ansatz
examples.translation: ansatz de evolución del Hamiltoniano de Heisenberg unidimensional
examples.suggested: ansatz de evolución del hamiltoniano de Heisenberg unidimensional
examples.why: Spanish convention writes 'hamiltoniano' in lowercase as a common noun.

editor_note: Entry 10 is faithful and reads naturally, with nothing added and no caveat dropped: "superficies de energía potencial", "rutas de reacción" and "información a nivel molecular" carry the English meaning, and "procesos químicos más eficientes en el uso de recursos" keeps the scope of the claim unchanged.

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The key caveats survive intact: two-qubit errors sit "por encima" of the reported ones because of crosstalk, T2 sits "por debajo", and a gap "no es automáticamente evidencia de deriva". The problem is terminology consistency. "Gate" is "puerta" in [0] but "compuerta" everywhere else. "Randomized benchmarking" is "evaluación comparativa aleatorizada" in [7] but "benchmarking aleatorizado" in [21], [51] and [52]. [16] also drops the hedge "about" (once a day).

examples.source: up-to-date T1, T2, readout, and gate errors
examples.translation: valores actualizados de T1, T2, lectura y errores de puerta
examples.suggested: valores actualizados de T1, T2, errores de lectura y de compuerta
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'compuerta' (e.g. [21], [22], [57]). 'puerta' appears only here.

examples.source: single-qubit randomized benchmarking, layered two-qubit randomized benchmarking
examples.translation: evaluación comparativa aleatorizada de un solo qubit, evaluación comparativa aleatorizada de dos qubits en capas
examples.suggested: benchmarking aleatorizado de un qubit, benchmarking aleatorizado de dos qubits en capas
examples.why: Entries [21], [51] and [52] call the same technique 'benchmarking aleatorizado (RB)'. Two names for one method is inconsistent.

examples.source: calibration procedures that typically run about once a day
examples.translation: procedimientos de calibración que típicamente se ejecutan una vez al día
examples.suggested: que normalmente se ejecutan aproximadamente una vez al día
examples.why: This drops the qualifier 'about'. It is a small hedge, and 'típicamente' is also a slight calque of 'typically'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful throughout. The key caveats come through intact: the result is 23.7 kcal/mol above the reference and misses chemical accuracy, and the removed opposite-spin interactions are still mentioned. 'HPC schedulers' is rendered two ways. The learning outcomes [6] and [9] use 'programadores de HPC', which reads as 'HPC programmers', while [21], [28], [65] and others use the correct 'planificadores'. 'Raw lifecycle' in [63] becomes 'ciclo de vida sin procesar' ('unprocessed lifecycle'), which is a calque. SQD is also split between 'basada en muestreo' ([10], [15]) and 'basada en muestras' ([81], [82]).

examples.source: How HPC schedulers (Slurm) inject quantum resources via environment variables
examples.translation: Cómo los programadores de HPC (Slurm) inyectan recursos cuánticos mediante variables de entorno
examples.suggested: Cómo los planificadores de HPC (Slurm) inyectan recursos cuánticos mediante variables de entorno
examples.why: 'programadores' reads as people (programmers). The rest of the file correctly uses 'planificadores' for scheduler, so the term is also inconsistent. Entry [6] has the same problem.

examples.source: The raw lifecycle above provides explicit control over every call.
examples.translation: El ciclo de vida sin procesar anterior ofrece un control explícito sobre cada llamada.
examples.suggested: El ciclo de vida de bajo nivel anterior ofrece un control explícito sobre cada llamada.
examples.why: 'Raw' here means direct or low-level API use, not unprocessed data. 'sin procesar' is a calque that doesn't make sense for a lifecycle.

examples.source: Sample-based quantum diagonalization tutorial
examples.translation: Tutorial de diagonalización cuántica basada en muestras
examples.suggested: Tutorial de diagonalización cuántica basada en muestreo
examples.why: The method name is inconsistent: entries [10] and [15] use 'basada en muestreo'. Entry [82] also uses 'muestras'.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The zig-zag mapping in [27], the pass-manager and warning behaviour in [51], and the three parameter changes in [66] all match the English. Three things are worth fixing. First, 'gate' is 'puertas' in [27] and [51] but 'compuerta' in [66] ('errores de compuerta'). Second, [51] translates 'layout' as 'diseño', which reads as visual design rather than a qubit layout; 'disposición' or 'layout' would be better. Third, 'siendo la conexión facilitada por un qubit auxiliar' in [27] is a stiff passive calque.

examples.source: Lower `n_reps` to `1` to reduce noise from gate errors
examples.translation: Reducir `n_reps` a `1` para disminuir el ruido de los errores de compuerta
examples.suggested: Reducir `n_reps` a `1` para disminuir el ruido de los errores de puerta
examples.why: The same file uses 'puertas' for gate in [27] ('puertas SWAP') and [51] ('conjunto de puertas'), so this is a within-file inconsistency.

examples.source: according to a "ladder" layout ... minimize the errors associated with the selected layout
examples.translation: según un diseño de "escalera" ... asociados con el diseño seleccionado
examples.suggested: según una disposición (layout) de "escalera" ... asociados con la disposición seleccionada
examples.why: Here 'layout' means how virtual qubits are assigned to physical qubits. 'Diseño' suggests visual design, while 'disposición' or the kept term 'layout' is the usual Qiskit rendering.

examples.source: with the connection being facilitated by an ancilla qubit (purple circles)
examples.translation: siendo la conexión facilitada por un qubit auxiliar (círculos morados)
examples.suggested: conexión que se realiza mediante un qubit auxiliar (círculos morados)
examples.why: A gerund plus passive is a calque of the English structure. A native technical writer would use a relative clause or 'mediante'.

editor_note: Entry 7 is faithful and reads naturally, with no drift or dropped caveats: "generación renovable variable y una demanda cambiante", "condiciones de operación" and "flujo de trabajo híbrido de clasificación cuántico-clásico" all match the English, and the hedge "puede apoyar el desarrollo de herramientas" keeps the source's modest claim.

The meaning holds throughout, including the subtle caveats in [59] (the filter changes the evolved operator, but the classical diagonalization still uses the full Hamiltonian) and [91] (skipping pruning is preferable on hardware), so nothing here would mislead a learner. There are some consistency and naturalness slips. 'Hamiltonian' is lowercase 'hamiltoniano' in [16]-[23] but 'Hamiltoniano' from [44] onward. 'Transpiler pass' is 'pases' in [17] but 'pasadas' everywhere else. 'Shallower circuits' is rendered as the calque 'circuitos más superficiales' in [68]. Smaller calques: 'contribuye una fase global' in [56], and the step headings switch between an imperative ('Mapea', [36]) and infinitives ('Optimizar', [66]).

examples.source: fermionic layout and synthesis passes
examples.translation: pases de layout y síntesis fermiónicos
examples.suggested: pasadas de layout y síntesis fermiónicas
examples.why: Everywhere else the file uses 'pasada(s)' for transpiler passes ([47], [49], [71]-[76]).

examples.source: the target Hamiltonian
examples.translation: del hamiltoniano objetivo
examples.suggested: del Hamiltoniano objetivo (or lowercase throughout)
examples.why: The capitalization is inconsistent: it is lowercase in [16]-[23] and capitalized from [44] on. Pick one convention.

examples.source: We can now create shallower circuits
examples.translation: Ahora podemos crear circuitos más superficiales
examples.suggested: Ahora podemos crear circuitos menos profundos
examples.why: 'Superficial' is a calque for circuit depth. The usual phrasing is 'menos profundo' or 'de menor profundidad', which the file itself uses in [8].

examples.source: whose time evolution contributes only a global phase
examples.translation: cuya evolución temporal solo contribuye una fase global
examples.suggested: cuya evolución temporal solo aporta una fase global
examples.why: 'Contribuir' used transitively like this is an anglicism. 'Aportar' is the natural verb.

examples.source: Step 1: Map classical inputs to a quantum problem
examples.translation: Paso 1: Mapea las entradas clásicas a un problema cuántico
examples.suggested: Paso 1: Mapear las entradas clásicas a un problema cuántico
examples.why: Steps 2-4 ([66], [78], [80]) use infinitives. Step 1 alone uses an imperative, so the parallel headings don't match.
